newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BOSKALIS' 96 TURNOVER UP, BUT OPERATING RESULT DOWN.
newsitem.headline: BOSKALIS' 96 TURNOVER UP, BUT OPERATING RESULT DOWN.

text.p: Dutch dredger Boskalis said on Thursday turnover from work done rose to record levels in 1996, but that growth had mainly been generated by acquisitions.
"The autonomous growth for dredging was very small, and capacity utilization remained unchanged from 1995," chairman Rob van Gelder told a results news conference.
Turnover from work done rose to 1.26 billion guilders in 1996 from a year-earlier 1.09 billion, while turnover on completed contracts rose to 1.15 billion from 1.10 billion.
However operating profits fell to 62.9 million guilders from a year-earlier 68.0 million, despite lower writedowns on equipment.
He said an upturn in the 1996 second half had been unable to offset a poor first half, when margins were squeezed by business taken on in 1995 when price competition was severe.
Van Gelder said the decline in first half operating profits had been slightly offset by income from projects completed in previous years that had been in dispute.
Such settlements were not booked until paid, he said, adding the sums in question were "relatively small items".
He said interest income had fallen due to the investment in the WD Fairway, which had eaten into Boskalis' cash position.
"As a result of this and lower interest rates, interest gains fell (to 2.6 million guilders from a year-earlier 6.6 million)," he said.
